<h1>Optimizing Compiler</h1>
</div>
<nav>
<a href="/">About</a>
<a href="/blog/">Blog</a>
<a href="/projects/">Projects</a>
</nav>
</header>

Built with [Viraj Shah](https://virajshah.vercel.app/). 

I built an optimizing L4 compiler in Rust end to end: parsing and elaboration, typechecking with a string interner, lowering to an SSA IR tree, translation to LLVM-like SSA, 3-address x86 SSA, and a backend with dominator analysis, if-conversion, graph-coloring register allocation, SSA deconstruction, and AT&T x86 emission. On the optimization side, I implemented early IR cleanup (copy and constant propagation, folding, DCE), repeated LLVM scalar passes (CSE, arithmetic strength reduction, branch folding), function inlining, tail-call elimination, LICM, partial redundancy elimination, induction-variable strength reduction, scalar replacement, and final x86 peepholes. I tuned the pipeline with per-pass ablations on hot benchmarks. Our O1 pipeline reaches over 70% of optimized GCC.

We built an end-to-end [C0](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~c0/docs/c0-reference.pdf) to x86-64 compiler. C0 is a safe subset of C, used in the introductory programming [class](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~15122/) at CMU

[Read the report (PDF)](l4-compiler-report.pdf)

The compiler passes code through five stages: source text &rarr; syntax tree &rarr; an SSA intermediate form (SSA just means each variable is assigned exactly once, which makes it much easier to reason about what a value is) &rarr; a simpler x86-like SSA form &rarr; final x86-64 machine code. Optimizations are applied along the way, but only when they're turned on (the "-O1" build below) — the unoptimized "-O0" build skips them.

To see which of these optimizations actually mattered, we tried disabling each one individually and re-measured runtime (in CPU cycles) on one of our benchmark programs — a numeric, recursion-heavy test case that exercises most of the optimizer at once:

<figure style="margin: 28px 0;">
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 300" width="100%" style="max-width: 640px; display: block; margin: 0 auto;" role="img" aria-label="Bar chart: effect of disabling each optimization, in millions of CPU cycles. Strength reduction plus 822.2 million, scalar cleanup plus 170.6 million, function inlining minus 65.0 million, if-conversion minus 36.9 million, register allocation tweak plus 10.1 million, final x86 cleanup plus 3.2 million">
<line x1="230" y1="14" x2="230" y2="280" stroke="#607058" stroke-width="1"/>

<text x="586" y="41" font-family="JetBrains Mono, monospace" font-size="11" fill="#1a2818">+822.2M</text>

<text x="196.3" y="129" font-family="JetBrains Mono, monospace" font-size="11" fill="#1a2818" text-anchor="end">-65.0M</text>

<text x="220" y="173" font-family="JetBrains Mono, monospace" font-size="11" fill="#1a2818" text-anchor="end">if-conversion</text>
<rect x="214.3" y="157" width="15.7" height="24" fill="#8c3050"/>
<text x="208.3" y="173" font-family="JetBrains Mono, monospace" font-size="11" fill="#1a2818" text-anchor="end">-36.9M</text>

<ul style="font-size: 14px; color: var(--text-dim); line-height: 1.6; max-width: 480px; margin: -8px auto 32px; padding-left: 20px;">
<li><strong style="color: var(--text);">strength reduction</strong> — replacing expensive multiply/divide with cheaper shifts and adds</li>
<li><strong style="color: var(--text);">scalar cleanup</strong> — constant folding, copy propagation, dead-code removal</li>
<li><strong style="color: var(--text);">function inlining</strong> — replacing a function call with the function's own body, to remove call overhead</li>
<li><strong style="color: var(--text);">if-conversion</strong> — turning small branches into branch-free instructions, so the CPU doesn't have to guess which way a branch goes</li>
<li><strong style="color: var(--text);">register allocation tweak</strong> — a heuristic for choosing which values live in fast CPU registers vs. slower memory</li>
<li><strong style="color: var(--text);">final x86 cleanup</strong> — small local rewrites to the generated assembly, like removing a jump to the very next instruction</li>
</ul>
